log.msg: item 0 done: ext/Chat/Mic.js, two fixes. (1) SETTINGS.sentences_per_send default 0->1 (line ~15): with 0, arm() always called check_chunk() instead of send_sentences(n), so nothing was ever sent sentence-by-sentence while listening -- only a big single flush at the 1200-char/60s safety ceiling. (2) send_sentences()'s n=Infinity safety path (called only by check_chunk()) always hit its own early-return `sents.length < n` -- any finite sents.length is < Infinity -- so the safety chunk described in its own comment never actually fired; fixed to skip that check when n===Infinity, and added a fallback (sents=[joined]) for when cut_re() finds no sentence-ending mark at all, so a punctuation-less run-on still flushes instead of growing forever.

Root cause, matching the owner's 20:40 evidence (session.jsonl, 3463 chars, one line, to:'same'): with sentences_per_send=0 (the old default) AND the Infinity-guard bug, a continuous dictation had no path that ever cut it before stop() -- not punctuation alone, a logic bug in the safety net itself.

Proof: ext/Chat/sentence-send.test.mjs, 7/7 PASS. One held item 'Sentence one. Sentence two. Sentence three.' -> 3 separate delivered messages in order (send_sentences default n=1). An unfinished tail with no closing mark stays held, not sent early. A ~1100-char punctuation-less run-on past the (lowered-for-the-test) chunk_chars floor flushes whole as one message via check_chunk(), nothing left behind.

Not yet touched: the receiving side's paragraph grouping (to:'same' vs a new paragraph) in the voice seat/Session -- the brief's own note that auto_check's paragraph_pause_ms must still let a mid-thought pause build one paragraph is about that grouping, unchanged here; this item only fixed the composer's send path. Items 1-3 (dimmer ink, V2 guess, paragraph breaks) still to do.

owner item 34 done: ux/Dictate/doc/status-icons.md written (verified against code), linked from ux/Dictate/readme.md. Covers the check (cursors.js:8, --ok green) and the brain (cursors.js:10, --warn) per piece/Prompt, plus v2's separate bottom smart-dots (ChatV2.js:68) and a reply's own static brain avatar (ChatV2.js:302, ChatV3.js:81) which are NOT the same marks.

Real finding (not fixed -- not a one-liner): V1's brain (Chat.js:125-130) colours 'done' as soon as smart has RECEIVED the chunk (sent.smart set); v2's brain (ChatV2.js:233-236, smart_answered() at :220) only colours once smart has actually ANSWERED (a title/text or a reply/question/task after sent.smart). Same icon, two different definitions of done -- this is the real source of 'out of sync', not clock drift. Fix would be: give V1's place_live_cursors() a way to check, from a live piece alone, whether an answer landed after sent.smart (same test v2's smart_answered() runs) -- needs a per-piece answer signal V1 doesn't currently have, so more than a one-line change; logged for the owner/next task to decide, not applied.
Side question: yes, a fast assistant runs on this session (since 19:22) -- as told by mastermind-dictation-v3, not independently re-verified here.

item 3 done (V1 side; V3's piece handed to mastermind-v3-messages, its own rebuild). Found THREE existing, disagreeing paragraph mechanisms: (1) ext/Chat/Chat.js mergeable()/MERGE_GAP_MS=8000ms -- the one that actually runs for V1's real chat, gap-based already, just needed item 0's separate sends to have a real gap to measure; no code change needed here. (2) ext/Refine/Placement.js's fallback decider -- text-only rules (question/cue-word/else unsure-forever), so a cue-word-less run-on never broke; fixed with a gap_ms param: 2s+ pause with no cue word now decides 'new' instead of 'unsure: append'. ext/Refine/RefineSystem.js now tracks the real gap between sends and feeds it in (today only wired on the Refine demo page, not yet the live voice-assistant's own fallback -- noted, not claimed as fixed end-to-end). (3) ChatV3.paragraphs() -- a flat group-every-3 heuristic on p.raw, ignoring p.cleaned's real Paragraphs list entirely; left untouched, mastermind-v3-messages owns V3's paragraph breaks in their session.messages rebuild (coordinated directly, no collision).
Also fixed (one-liner): ux/Dictate/doc/chat.md said MERGE_GAP_MS was 10s; the code says 8000ms (Chat.js:12). Corrected.

Decision + alternative written in ux/Dictate/doc/chat.md ('Paragraphs at a pause'): the client decides WHEN to send (item 0), never whether a paragraph breaks -- that stays with whichever layer draws/places the sentence (mergeable() for V1, Placement's fallback soon the voice assistant). Alternative considered and rejected: the client tags each send new_paragraph itself -- would duplicate the pause judgement in a second place that can't see the voice assistant's own topic reasoning, the same two-signals-one-thing shape item 34 found in the check/brain pair.

Proof: ext/Refine/test/Placement.test.mjs (7 checks incl. the new gap-aware case) and ext/Refine/test/paragraph-pauses.test.mjs (6/6) -- a 6-sentence rambling dictation, no question marks, no cue words, two real pauses (2.8s, 3.1s) among short ones (0.3-0.5s): lands in 3 paragraphs, not 1, nothing lost. V1's own draw-side (split_paragraph()) was already proven live elsewhere (ux/Dictate/test/in-place.mjs, doc/voice-assistant.md); not re-proven here.
